requirements.requirement: Create an encrypted (LUKS) volume on node1
requirements.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 succeeded on a file-backed container at /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img, luksOpen mapped it as /dev/mapper/secure, and luksDump confirms LUKS2 header with aes-xts-plain64 cipher.

requirements.requirement: Volume is formatted with a filesystem and mounted at /srv/secure
requirements.summary: mkfs.xfs formatted /dev/mapper/secure; mount -a mounted it at /srv/secure and a test file was written/read back; post-reboot check confirms the same mountpoint and filesystem.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks automatically at boot without manual passphrase entry
requirements.summary: An /etc/crypttab entry referencing the container by file path with a root-only keyfile (luks,nofail) was added and corrected to remove an inapplicable UUID= reference; systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service started purely from this crypttab entry (no manual cryptsetup invocation), and after a real reboot (boot_id changed) the service was active again automatically.

An /etc/fstab entry (/dev/mapper/secure /srv/secure xfs defaults,nofail 0 2) was added; after the observed reboot, /srv/secure was mounted and the pre-reboot healthcheck.txt content matched exactly, demonstrating unattended mount and data persistence across the actual restart.

overall_summary: The executor built a LUKS2-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1, mounted it at /srv/secure, and configured crypttab/fstab with a root-only keyfile for unattended boot-time unlock and mount. This was directly validated by a real reboot: boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and post-restart evidence shows the cryptsetup service active, the volume mounted, and pre-reboot data intact. All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and no unresolved hygiene issues remain.
limitations: The initial crypttab entry momentarily used an inapplicable UUID= reference before being corrected within the same short attempt; this is documented as a self-corrected drafting error rather than residual misconfiguration, but is noted for completeness.
Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so the provider-wide restart protocol coverage is limited to a single node by design, not by omission.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline is clean overall. One minor self-correction occurred: cmd-63840f2f53fc440b initially wrote a crypttab entry using 'UUID=' (inapplicable to a file-backed LUKS container) which was immediately deleted and replaced with a correct path-based entry in cmd-1c6fea9abcae443c, leaving no residue in the final /etc/crypttab (verified single-line file in cmd-a15f83013db44cee). cmd-f4340f7231764645 unmounted/closed the volume only to restart the cryptsetup unit cleanly after the crypttab fix, a bounded and necessary step to validate the corrected config before reboot. The provider-wide node-restart protocol was executed on the only managed node (node1): pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline captured (cmd-8a4b1aa278d4458d), reboot acknowledged (cmd-4f763bb44fbc4b1f), a different post-restart boot_id observed (cmd-a44cb3903afc4285), and recovered service/mount/data state confirmed (cmd-0e64a6697c2243da). Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate: boot-identity changed from f455a75c... to 4dea6efc..., no new failed services, no package-health regressions, and only expected transient /tmp entries changed.
